findings.message: The fix only handles part of the fenced-code case. `stray()` treats only a line starting with three backticks as a fence. Three variants are wrong: (1) a `~~~` fence is not recognised, so a documented `extends: node` inside it is reported as an error, which is a false positive that blocks the whole build. (2) Every line is `.strip()`ped before the check, so an indented code block or an indented list continuation line `    extends: node` is also flagged. (3) An unclosed ``` fence hides every later line, so a real stray `extends:` after it is silently ignored. That is the fail-open case this fix was meant to close. Track the fence character and length, and close only on a matching fence. Check the indentation-sensitive form on the raw line instead of the stripped one. Warn when a fence is still open at end of file.
findings.scenario:
A preset body containing '~~~
extends: node
~~~' -> warn and exit 1 (false positive). A body with '```
text
' never closed, then 'extends: node' -> exit 0 with no warning, and the local file silently replaces the built-in.

findings.message: The variant table for the stray-`extends:` check covers only the backtick fence. It has no rows for a `~~~` fence, an indented `extends:` line, an unclosed fence followed by `extends:`, `Extends : node` with a space before the colon, or a heading containing the word. Without these rows the instance fix above passes while the variants misbehave. Add them to the table.

findings.message: The README says an `extends:` line outside frontmatter is an error. It does not say that lines inside a fenced code block are exempt, so the doc and the code disagree. State the fence exemption, or narrow the code to match the doc.
findings.scenario: A reader following the README puts an example `extends: node` in a code fence and cannot tell whether it is allowed.
